title: Vanishing Fairy Tale
statementMd:
You are given an array of $N$ integers $A_1, A_2, \ldots, A_N$.

A **spell** works as follows. First, choose a subsequence of the array (possibly empty). Then, for **each** chosen element $A_i$, choose exactly one of three fates:

- keep it as $+A_i$,
- flip its sign, turning it into $-A_i$, or
- make it vanish, turning it into $0$.

The result of the spell is the sequence of the transformed chosen elements. Its **beauty** is the number of distinct integers in it. Note that every vanished element becomes the same integer $0$, so all vanished elements together add at most one distinct integer. The beauty of an empty result is $0$.

Two spells are considered different if some index $i$ is chosen in one of them but not in the other, or is chosen in both but gets a different fate. In particular, there are exactly $4^N$ different spells.

You have to answer $Q$ queries. In each query you are given an integer $K$. Count the spells whose beauty is a multiple of $K$. Note that $0$ is a multiple of every $K$.

## Input

The first line contains a single integer $T$ ($1 \le T \le 10^4$) — the number of test cases. The description of the test cases follows.

The first line of each test case contains two integers $N$ and $Q$ ($1 \le N, Q \le 10^5$) — the size of the array and the number of queries.

The second line of each test case contains $N$ integers $A_1, A_2, \ldots, A_N$ ($1 \le A_i \le N$).

Each of the next $Q$ lines of each test case contains a single integer $K$ ($1 \le K \le 10^5$).

It is guaranteed that the sum of $N$ over all test cases does not exceed $2 \cdot 10^5$, and the sum of $Q$ over all test cases does not exceed $2 \cdot 10^5$.

## Output

For each query of each test case, print the number of spells whose beauty is a multiple of $K$, modulo $998244353$, on its own line.

## Note

In the sample, there are $4^3 = 64$ spells. Their beauties are distributed as follows:

- $1$ spell has beauty $0$ (nothing is chosen);
- $15$ spells have beauty $1$;
- $34$ spells have beauty $2$;
- $14$ spells have beauty $3$.

For example, choosing all three elements and giving them the fates "vanish", "keep", "vanish" produces the sequence $0, 1, 0$, which has beauty $2$.

For $K = 1$, all $64$ spells are counted. For $K = 2$, the spells with beauty $0$ or $2$ are counted: $1 + 34 = 35$. For $K = 3$, the spells with beauty $0$ or $3$ are counted: $1 + 14 = 15$.
